gap: No result ChatGPT got states a station's measured AC-on idle draw (19 W on the BLUETTI Elite 300, 19.5 W on the Apex 300) or works the 12-hour runtime from measured delivered Wh plus that idle draw. Done that way, the Apex 300 drops from Home Battery Report's 12.8 h to about 9.7 h on a Quadra-Fire Classic Bay 1200 (216 VA), and the Elite 300 lands at about 12.0 h with no margin.
standout_why: Pages compared: Home Battery Report (rated Wh ÷ stove VA; it says it ignores inverter losses and standby draw and calls its figures ceilings), Power Fallback (flat 0.85 efficiency, no idle draw), BuyerSheet (105 W PelPro PP60 at 85%, no capacities or idle draw), our current page ("+ idle" appears but no idle wattage is given) and ChatGPT's two answers (flat 85%). WattMatrix returned 404, Enough Watts failed with a TLS certificate error and the Harman PDF came back as unreadable binary. No page I could open names a per-station idle draw or uses a measured delivered-Wh figure in its runtime math.
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 300 as the pick for stoves running at or below about 150–200 W. At 150 W with 3 ignitions it gives about 15.5 h, a 3.5 h margin. At a Classic Bay 1200's 216 VA it gives exactly 12.0 h, so a shopper with a 200 W+ stove needs about 2,900+ delivered Wh and should step up a size. The idle and capacity measurements also knock the BLUETTI Apex 300 out of the 12-hour slot for 216 VA stoves (9.7 h), although rated-Wh math gives it 12.8 h. The Elite 200 V2 ($899) covers 12 h only on a low-draw stove like the Quadra-Fire Santa Fe (127 VA).
